cli.audit.two_topics: rules and decisions whose 「A — B」 title glues two topics: %d (split candidates):
cli.audit.policy: Thresholds: confirmSeenDays %d · confirmFollowedVerified %d · correctionRepeatSessions %d (the last two wait for your decision, E2)
cli.backup.busy: another backup is running; try again in a moment
cli.backup.restore.done: Restored from %s (%d memories). The DB before it: %s
cli.backup.restore.keep: The DB as it is now is kept first as before-restore-*.sqlite in %s.
cli.backup.restore.need_yes: Nothing changed. Run it again with --yes to restore.
cli.backup.status.due: The next session start makes a copy (the last one is 24 hours old or more)
cli.backup.status.next: Next automatic copy: a session start after %s
cli.backup.status.others: Old work log copies: %d, copies before a schema change·restore·import·migrate: %d
cli.doctor.fix.codex_hooks: in Codex, open /hooks and trust orbit-mem's hooks
cli.doctor.fix.codex_memories: %s (sets features.memories, memories.generate_memories and memories.use_memories false in %s)
cli.doctor.head:
orbit-mem %s (%s, %s/%s)
Data: %s
cli.doctor.language: Language: %s (orbit-mem config set language en|ko, or ORBIT_LANG)
cli.doctor.memories: Memories: confirmed %d · candidate %d · stale %d · hidden %d · %d proposals waiting
cli.doctor.path_binary: orbit-mem on PATH (the hooks and MCP server call it): %s

cli.ledger.empty: The ledger is empty. Each approved proposal adds a line.
cli.ledger.observation: Observed: before bad signals %d · irrelevant %d · sessions %d → after %d · %d · %d
cli.migrate.done: Of %d old records, migrated %d. Already migrated: %d.
cli.migrate.done_dry: Of %d old records, %d can be migrated (preview). Already migrated: %d.

cli.migrate.reindexed: Rebuilt the search index from %d memories.
cli.migrate.index_filled: Filled the search index for %d late memories.

cli.migrate.sources: %d sources. File evidence: same %d · changed %d · unknown %d. %d memories to judge again. %d marked absorbed.
cli.proposals.drain_dry: (preview on a copy) %d pending proposals: %d would be applied by the automatic rules, %d closed without applying. To do it, run orbit-mem backup, then again without --dry-run.
cli.proposals.drain_left: %d left pending (a transient error, or a file-writing change a preview does not run). Run again to retry.
cli.proposals.drained: Closed %d pending proposals: %d applied by the automatic rules, %d closed without applying. The rows stay; undo from the audit list.
cli.proposals.list_tail: %d pending. The approval queue is gone — close what is left with orbit-mem proposals drain. Details: orbit-mem proposals show <id>
cli.proposals.review_prompt: approve a · reject r · skip s · quit q
cli.uninstall.done: Took the %s plugin out of the hosts. Kept the memory DB, the activity log, backups and the local plugin folder: %s
cli.uninstall.err.partial: some parts were not removed; see the errors above. The memory DB is untouched: %s
cli.uninstall.host_error: %s: error while taking the plugin out: %v
cli.usage_head:
orbit-mem — shared AI memory and activity log for this PC

Commands:
flag.activity.project: all for every project; a project directory; default this project
flag.activity.since: only activity since YYYY-MM-DD, an RFC 3339 time, or 7d / 12h ago
flag.audit.days: days of automatic changes to show
flag.backup.yes: restore without asking (the change is printed first)
flag.edit.link: id of a memory to link (repeatable)
flag.edit.title: new title
flag.edit.unlink: id of a linked memory to unlink (repeatable)
flag.export.out: file (jsonl) or folder (md); without it jsonl goes to stdout
flag.import.dry_run: only check what would be imported
flag.inject.cwd: working directory that picks the project scope
flag.inject.host: host name recorded with the use event
flag.inject.session: session id, to keep the session bundle stable
flag.inject.source: how the session started (startup, resume, compact, clear): compact and clear make the bundle anew
flag.install.dry_run: only show what would be done
flag.install.local_plugin: register Claude Code from the local plugin folder this orbit-mem builds, not the GitHub marketplace
flag.install.marketplace: marketplace source the Claude Code plugin comes from: owner/repo, a git URL, or a local folder (kept as setting claudeMarketplace; default crispebble/orbit-mem)
flag.install.no_hosts: do not build or register the plugin in Claude Code and Codex
flag.mcp.actor: who writes through this server: ai (default), user (a person), automation
flag.memory.state: state candidate|confirmed|stale|hidden (repeatable; default candidate and confirmed)
flag.migrate.from: copy of the old Knowledge SQLite
flag.migrate.reindex: empty the search index and build it again from every memory
flag.plugin.out: folder for both host formats and both local marketplaces (default: $ORBIT_HOME/plugins/orbit-mem)
flag.plugin.repo: repository root to write the GitHub marketplace into (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and plugin/, Claude Code format)
flag.proposals.body_file: file with the body to approve with
flag.proposals.dry_run: preview on a copy without changing the real database
flag.proposals.title: title to approve with
flag.stats.days: number of days up to today
usage.activity: orbit-mem activity [query] [--host H] [--project all|DIR] [--since DATE] [-n N] [--json]   # session activity log (activity_find)
usage.audit: orbit-mem audit [--days N] [--json] | audit revert <ledger-or-proposal-id> [--note] | audit dismiss <f-…|correction:…>   # audit list: automatic confirmations and clean-ups, conflicts, repeated corrections
usage.backup: orbit-mem backup [list|status|restore <copy> [--yes]]   # copy the memory DB now · list copies · their state · restore one
usage.edit: orbit-mem edit <id> [--title T] [--body B | --body-file F] [--tag T]... [--link ID]... [--unlink ID]... [--note N] [--json]   # fix a memory (memory_update)
usage.export: orbit-mem export [--format jsonl|md] [--out PATH] [--all]   # jsonl to stdout, or Markdown files in a folder
usage.hook: orbit-mem hook session-start|prompt|pre-tool|subagent-start|session-end --host claude|codex   # host hooks (stdin JSON): memory context and the activity log
usage.import: orbit-mem import <file.jsonl> [--dry-run] [--json]   # add exported memories; ids already there are skipped
usage.inject: orbit-mem inject session-start|prompt --host H [--cwd DIR] [--session ID] [--rules brief|full]   # memory context as JSON (prompt on stdin) for a host without hooks; inject delivered --host H --session S --ids A,B records the memories the host put into a model request
usage.ledger: orbit-mem ledger [--all] [--n N] [--json]   # approved changes and their effect verdicts
usage.list: orbit-mem list [--kind K]... [--state S]... [--tag T]... [--all] [-n N] [--json]   # recent memories
usage.mcp: orbit-mem mcp [--actor ai|user|automation]   # MCP server the hosts start (stdio): memory tools and activity_find
usage.migrate:
orbit-mem migrate [--json]   (schema migration, fills late search index rows)
       orbit-mem migrate --reindex [--json]   (build the search index again)
       orbit-mem migrate --from <copy of knowledge-auto-*.sqlite> [--dry-run] [--json]
usage.plugin: orbit-mem plugin build [--out D | --repo R]   # orbit-mem's own Claude Code and Codex plugin
usage.proposals: orbit-mem proposals [list|show <id>|drain [--dry-run]|approve <id> [--title T] [--body B|--body-file F] [--note N]|reject <id> [--note N]|review] [--all] [--json]
usage.search: orbit-mem search <query> [--kind K]... [--all] [--stale] [-n N] [--json]   # find memories (memory_find)
usage.stale: orbit-mem stale <id> [--note N] [--json]   # mark a memory stale (kept, not deleted)
usage.stats: orbit-mem stats [--days N | --week YYYY-MM-DD (a Monday)] [--json]   # corrections, recall, use verdicts, ledger and proposal metrics
usage.uninstall: orbit-mem uninstall   # removes the plugin from the hosts; keeps the memory DB
flag.inject.rules: brief or full, accepted so older calls keep working; it has no effect (the confirmed rules are always in full)
flag.inject.ids: delivered: memory ids the host put into the model request, comma separated
usage.tool: orbit-mem tool memory_find|memory_get|memory_save|memory_update|activity_find --host H [--cwd DIR] [--session ID] [--actor ai]   # a memory tool for a host without MCP: MCP input JSON on stdin, output JSON on stdout
cli.tool.no_db: there is no memory database yet (save a memory first, or run orbit-mem install)
usage.why: orbit-mem why <memory id> [request words…] [--cwd DIR] [--host H] [--session S] [--rules brief|full] [--json]   # why a memory did not reach a request: stored, eligible, selected, injected, delivered, used
cli.why.head: Why %s (%s)
cli.why.session_rule: a confirmed rule: it goes in at session start, not with each request
cli.why.out_of_scope: out of scope: the memory is %s, this session is %s
cli.why.journal: a journal entry, never recalled into a conversation
cli.why.expired: a volatile memory that ran out on %s
cli.why.superseded: an older value: %s is the newest of topic %s
cli.why.no_prompt: give the request words to judge this
cli.why.weak_match: under the thresholds: matched [%s] of [%s], find score %s (threshold %s), share of words %s (threshold %s); it needs two or more meaningful words and both values at their thresholds (recallMinScore, recallMinCoverage; recallMinCoverageOneWord when only one word matched)
cli.why.below_top: under the relative threshold: find score %s is below %s, the share (recallMinRelative %s) of the best match of this request
cli.why.would_inject: no record for a session; this request would put it in at rank %s
cli.why.would_inject_rules: no record for a session; a new session would put it in
cli.why.over_budget: matched but left out by the request recall's lines (%s) or length (%s characters)
cli.why.already_shown: already given in this session (request recall, correction or new memory line); a memory goes in once per session, and again after compact or clear
cli.why.skipped: not looked at: an earlier stage stopped
cli.why.delivered: the host put it into the model request (%s)
cli.why.hook_returned: the %s hook handed it to the host, which adds it to the request
cli.why.not_delivered: put in, but the host recorded no delivery (it was recalled earlier in the session, or the turn did not run)
cli.why.no_record: no record of putting it in for this session
cli.why.verdict_followed: the session-end review judged it followed
cli.why.verdict_violated: the session-end review judged it broken
cli.why.verdict_irrelevant: the session-end review judged it beside the point
cli.why.opened: the AI opened it with memory_get (%s)
cli.why.review_due: its review date %s passed: a stale candidate
cli.doctor.problem.claude-memory-plugin: The Claude Code memory plugin %s is on: memories split between it and orbit-mem
cli.hostmem.after: No memory files were deleted. New sessions of the host pick up the change.
cli.hostmem.ask.claude: Claude Code's own memory (auto memory) is on, so memories split between it and orbit-mem. Turn it off?
cli.hostmem.ask.codex: Codex's own memories are on, so memories split between them and orbit-mem. Turn them off?
cli.hostmem.ask.head: Check with the user (orbit-mem changed none of this; the user decides):
cli.hostmem.ask.plugin: The %s plugin %s (%s) keeps memories of its own, so memories split between it and orbit-mem. Turn it off?
cli.hostmem.ask.reason: Two memory systems save and recall the same things apart: a rule can come in twice, or an old version can come back after you changed it. Turning one off deletes no memory files, and orbit-mem host-memory on puts it back.
cli.hostmem.ask.tail: Why: %s To keep them all and not be asked again: %s
cli.hostmem.err.not_object: the settings file is not a JSON object
cli.hostmem.err.unknown: no such overlap here: %s (see orbit-mem host-memory status)
cli.hostmem.none: No other memory system found (Claude Code and Codex are not set up here).
cli.hostmem.note: Memory systems that overlap orbit-mem are on (%s). Ask the user whether to turn them off; turn off only what they agree to with `orbit-mem host-memory off --only <id>`. If they want to keep them, run `%s`.
cli.hostmem.on.kept: Left %s in %s: it was changed after orbit-mem turned it off.
cli.hostmem.on.nothing: orbit-mem turned nothing off, so there is nothing to put back.
cli.hostmem.status.setting: hostMemory: %s (keep = the user keeps them and is not asked again)
flag.hostmem.only: only these overlaps (ids from host-memory status, comma-separated)
flag.install.json: print the result as JSON with askUser: the questions to put to the user
usage.host-memory: orbit-mem host-memory [status|off|on] [--host claude|codex|all] [--only ID,...] [--json]   # memory systems that overlap orbit-mem: show them, turn them off (after the user agrees), put back what orbit-mem turned off
cli.hostmem.err.inline_table: %s is an inline table in config.toml (%s = { … }); it cannot be changed safely here. Ask the user to change it in Codex
cli.hostmem.ask.mcp: The %s MCP server %s (%s) keeps memories of its own, so memories split between it and orbit-mem. Turn it off?
cli.hostmem.ask.reason_locked: It is turned on in %s (project or managed settings, above the user settings), so orbit-mem does not change it. Whoever owns that file decides.
cli.hostmem.ask.reason_manual: orbit-mem does not change this host's MCP list: the command removes the server from it (its memories stay, and claude mcp add brings it back).
cli.hostmem.ask.line_locked: - %s It is kept on by %s; orbit-mem does not change that file.
cli.hostmem.status.locked: kept on by %s (above the user settings): off leaves it
cli.hostmem.off.locked: %s is kept on by %s; left as it is.
cli.hostmem.off.manual: %s is not turned off by orbit-mem. To turn it off: %s
cli.doctor.fix.locked: turned on in %s (project or managed settings); orbit-mem does not change it
cli.doctor.problem.claude-memory-mcp: The Claude Code MCP server %s (%s) keeps memories: memories split between it and orbit-mem
cli.doctor.problem.codex-memory-plugin: The Codex memory plugin %s is on: memories split between it and orbit-mem
cli.doctor.problem.codex-memory-mcp: The Codex MCP server %s (%s) keeps memories: memories split between it and orbit-mem
cli.doctor.problem.host-settings-unreada: Could not read %s for the overlapping memory check: %s
usage.update: orbit-mem update [--check] [--dry-run] [--version X] [--force] [--json]   # replace orbit-mem with the newest GitHub release (sha256 verified), then run its install
flag.update.check: only look up the newest version; change nothing
flag.update.dry_run: only show what would be done
flag.update.version: install this version instead of the newest
flag.update.json: print the result as JSON (ok, error, current, latest, updated, binary, steps)
cli.update.available: A newer orbit-mem is out: %s -> %s (orbit-mem update)
cli.doctor.update: Version: %s (newest known: %s, newer available: %s, update check: %s)
flag.update.force: allow --version to go to a version older than the current one
cli.update.err.no_path: cannot tell where the running orbit-mem file is (got %q); nothing was written
usage.place: orbit-mem place [--cwd DIR] [--json] | --suggest [--root DIR] [--json] | --move [--json] | --plan F [--dry-run] [--json]   # which product the product map (config products) gives a folder, a first map, moving product:? memories, applying a migration plan
flag.place.cwd: folder to look at (default: the current one)
cli.place.multi: Several products: %s (no product core at session start; a request that names one puts its memories first)
cli.place.none: No product: the product map (config products) has no line for this folder
cli.place.default: A memory saved here without appliesTo applies to: %s
cli.place.remote_hint: This is a git repository with a remote: the map finds it by its remote key, not by a folder line. Add "%s" to the product's match lines
flag.place.suggest: suggest a first product map from this PC's repository remotes and work folders (does not write the config)
flag.place.move: move the product:? memories the product map places to their product (automatic change, undone from the audit list)
cli.place.plan_head: migration plan of %d: applied %d · skipped %d · conflicts %d (dry run %v)
flag.place.dry_run: show what --plan would change without changing it
cli.place.journals_head: journals → activity log: moved %d · skipped %d (dry run %v)
flag.place.journals: move every live journal memory to the activity log and mark it stale (one ledger line each, S4-8)
flag.place.plan: apply a migration plan (JSON) an AI wrote: it changes applies-to, topic and supersession only, one ledger line per change (S4)
cli.place.suggest_next: Put it into config.json products and fix the wrong lines, then run orbit-mem place --move to move the trapped product:? memories (the daily tidy does too).
cli.place.moved: - %s · %s: product:?(%s) → %s (ledger %s, undo: orbit-mem audit revert <ledger id>)
usage.product: orbit-mem product rename OLD NEW [--dry-run] [--json]   # rename a product of the product map (config.json products) and move its memories (product:OLD) with it; backs up the memory DB and config.json first
flag.product.dry_run: show what would be renamed and moved without changing anything or making backups
cli.product.err.no_config: no configuration at %s: there is no product map to rename
cli.product.err.no_old: the product map has no product %q
cli.product.err.new_taken: the product map already has a product %q
cli.product.err.config_changed: %s changed while renaming; nothing was renamed, run the command again
cli.product.would_rename: Would rename %s → %s: config.json products and %d memories (dry run, nothing changed)
usage.core: orbit-mem core --suggest [--scope user|product:<name>] [--json] | --pin <id,…> [--quote "user's words"] [--json]   # suggest the first always-on core, pin the memories kept
flag.core.suggest: suggest, per layer, the confirmed memories to always keep within its limit (changes nothing)
flag.core.scope: layer to look at: user or product:<name> (default: user and every product layer)
flag.core.pin: ids of the memories to pin into the core (comma separated)
flag.core.quote: when an AI runs it (ORBIT_ACTOR=ai), the user's words that decided the pin, kept on memories holding the user's words. A person running it needs none
cli.core.apply: apply: orbit-mem core --pin %s  (drop the wrong ones; a person runs it. When an AI runs it (ORBIT_ACTOR=ai), memories holding the user's words need --quote with them)
usage.tidy: orbit-mem tidy [--json]   # run the daily model-free tidy now (the session-start hook runs it once a day)
cli.tidy.done: Tidied: judged %d, reverted %d harmful automatic changes, confirmed %d, closed %d proposals, marked %d expired and %d unused candidates stale, moved %d to products
cli.doctor.recall: Recall %s · work recall %d chars · daily tidy %s (last %s)
usage.host: orbit-mem host version|context|recall|tool-context|call|delivered|reset|session-end [--actor ai]   # host contract v1: one JSON request on stdin, one JSON result on stdout (exit 0 ok, 1 operation error, 2 usage error)
cli.host.err.timeout: the operation did not finish within its time limit
cli.host.err.no_db: there is no memory database yet (save a memory first, or run orbit-mem install)
cli.host.err.schema_newer: the memory database is newer than this orbit-mem (run orbit-mem update)
cli.host.err.schema_older: the memory database needs a schema migration (run orbit-mem migrate)
cli.host.err.unknown_tool: not a tool this contract calls: %s
cli.host.err.usage.input: usage error: the request is not one JSON object
cli.host.err.usage.bad_value: usage error: %s does not accept the value %q
cli.host.err.usage.missing: usage error: required fields are missing: %s
cli.host.err.contract: the contract version is not supported (the request is for version %s, this orbit-mem speaks version %s)
cli.host.err.contract_any: the contract version is not supported
cli.host.err.input_wait: the request on stdin did not end in time
cli.host.err.may_have_applied: The write may still have been applied: look with memory_find or memory_get before writing again.
cli.inject.schema_newer: the memory database is newer than this orbit-mem, so no memory context was given (run orbit-mem update)
cli.inject.schema_older: the memory database needs a schema migration, so no memory context was given (run orbit-mem migrate)
